questions.question: A medical test for a disease has the following characteristics: Probability of testing positive given the disease (True Positive Rate) = 0.95, Probability of testing negative given no disease (True Negative Rate) = 0.90, Prevalence of the disease in the population = 0.01. If a randomly selected person tests positive, what is the probability that they actually have the disease?
questions.explanation: Using Bayes’ Theorem: P(Disease|Positive) = [P(Positive|Disease) * P(Disease)] / [P(Positive|Disease) * P(Disease) + P(Positive|No Disease) * P(No Disease)] = (0.95 * 0.01) / (0.95 * 0.01 + 0.10 * 0.99) = 0.0095 / 0.1085 ≈ 0.087
questions.hint: Apply Bayes’ Theorem to calculate the posterior probability.

questions.explanation: The product of the slopes of the two regression lines is equal to r². Slope of Y on X = 3, slope of X on Y = 0.3. So r² = 3 × 0.3 = 0.9 → r = √0.9 ≈ 0.9487, which is closest to 0.9.
questions.hint: Recall that the product of the slopes of the regression lines equals r².
